column4: The day is both مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ and مَشْهُودٌ, placing the section's crowd-root and presence/witness-root together in the universal assembly.
يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ gives the gathering its Quranic name and makes that assembly the day when true gain and loss appear.
After people surge into one another, the trumpet sounds and God says فَجَمَعْنَاهُمْ جَمْعًا, exactly enlarging a confused crowd into the final collection.
One cry makes every person جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ; the ayah joins total gathering to being made present before God.
The trumpet sends people streaming from graves toward رَبِّهِمْ, turning the surah's rushing movement into resurrection's mass advance toward their Lord.
يَوْمَ الْجَمْعِ is named explicitly, and the one assembly resolves into two companies, one in the Garden and one in the Blaze.
The prayer addresses رَبَّنَا as جَامِعُ النَّاسِ for an unquestionable day, matching the section's movement from their Lord to all humanity gathered.
فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ describes an unquestionable day when every soul is paid fully, giving purpose to the section's universal collection.
God promises لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ and grounds it in His uniquely truthful speech, a direct formulation of the great gathering.
لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ follows the statement that mercy is written upon God, placing universal gathering under that lordly relation.
God gives life, causes death, then يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ, stating the whole movement into the assembly as one divine action.
لَمَجْمُوعُونَ إِلَى مِيقَاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ supplies the appointed day on which the former and latter named in 56:49 become one collected multitude.
الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ defines the full temporal span of the crowd that 56:50 says will be gathered at one known appointment.
هَذَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ جَمَعْنَاكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ combines the day, the present audience, and all earlier people in one judicial assembly.
Wherever people may be, يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا promises their convergence from every location into a single divine summons.
After the landscape is stripped bare, وَحَشَرْنَاهُمْ فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا makes explicit that no one remains outside the gathered crowd.
The people gathered in 18:47 are عُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا; this ayah supplies their ordered presence before the Lord after collection.
يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ depicts a particular assembly within the universal day and immediately questions its witnesses about their reception.
وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا stages everyone together before God, who then addresses the associators inside that assembled scene.
وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا gathers jinn and humans together, making the section's all-human scale still wider and exposing their relations.
وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا is followed by a command separating associators from their partners, so the undifferentiated crowd becomes a scene of disclosure.
God gathers them all, يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا, then questions the angels, joining universal presence with testimony about earthly allegiance.
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ names the section's Lord as the one who gathers them and closes with His wisdom and knowledge.
Every generation is جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ, joining the crowd-root with the section's developed sense of being present before God.
God swears by رَبِّكَ to gather humans and devils, then لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ around Hell, combining assembly with compulsory presence.
The earth splits from them as they emerge سِرَاعًا, and the ayah names the event حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ, a swift universal muster.
People come from graves سِرَاعًا and rush as if toward a marker, closely recasting the surah's charging motion as mass resurrection.
They leave graves like جَرَادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ; the one gathered humanity appears visually dispersed like locusts while moving toward one summons.
مُهْطِعِينَ إِلَى الدَّاعِ gives the scattered multitude of 54:7 its common direction: all hurry toward the caller on the hard day.
On the day the trumpet is blown, فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا depicts humanity arriving as successive crowds rather than the few tents of the raid.
زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ is enough for everyone suddenly to be looking, directly paralleling the single sound that completes the gathering in the section.
زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ supplies the single summons whose immediate result is the collective appearance described in 79:14.
فَإِذَا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ shows the multitude suddenly present on the open surface after the single blast of 79:13.
The command to listen for the caller from مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ introduces the common summons whose result 50:42 calls the day of emergence.
All hear الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ, and the ayah identifies it as يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ, the sounding that brings the buried crowd out.
Two trumpet blasts distinguish collapse from assembly: after the second, فَإِذَا هُمْ قِيَامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ, setting a sequence beside the section's single cry.
Between the grave-rush of 36:51 and collective presence of 36:53, the awakened crowd recognizes that the messengers' promised resurrection was true.
Once all are present in 36:53, this ayah states the result: no soul is wronged and each is repaid only for what it did.
God sends the warning to announce يَوْمَ التَّلَاقِ, another name for the day defined by everyone meeting in one divine presence.
On that Day of Meeting, هُمْ بَارِزُونَ and nothing about them is hidden from God, matching the collection of concealed contents.
يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَى مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ joins presentation before God to the disappearance of every hidden thing.
يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ makes the day specifically the testing and exposure of inner secrets, the closest thematic parallel to collecting what breasts contain.
God يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا, reports their deeds, has counted what they forgot, and is شَهِيدٌ over all: gathering, accounting, and witness converge.
أُمَّةً وَسَطًا ... شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ unites both roots developed by the section: being in the middle and bearing witness over humanity.
Jesus says he was شَهِيدًا only مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ; his witness depended on presence among the people, while God's witness continues after his departure.
In the assembled address to jinn and humans, شَهِدْنَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِنَا makes the gathered beings testify against themselves about meeting this day.
A witness is brought مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ and the Messenger is brought as witness over these people, populating the universal assembly with its witnesses.
يَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا makes every community present through a witness on the day when denials are no longer admitted.
The repeated scene raises فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا from among its own people and brings the Messenger as witness over his audience.
God draws مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا and demands proof, showing how the collected peoples become an evidentiary gathering.
In the illuminated judgment scene, وَجِيءَ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ brings prophets and witnesses into the assembled presence before judgment.
Every soul comes with a driver and شَهِيدٌ, assigning individual witness and escort to each member of the universal crowd.
شَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ pairs witness and witnessed immediately after the promised day of 85:2, echoing the section's gathering-place sense of witnessing.
الْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ supplies the eschatological day to which the witness and witnessed of 85:3 belong.
After the people are gathered and presented in 18:47-48, they find مَا عَمِلُوا حَاضِرًا; even their deeds are collected into presence.
On the day each soul finds its good and evil مُحْضَرًا, inward moral contents become present objects from which it cannot distance itself.
At the cosmic judgment, عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا أَحْضَرَتْ makes each soul know exactly what it has brought into presence.
وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ says God knows what they store within, tightly matching the section's collection of what breasts contain.
In the surah that names the Day of Gathering at 64:9, God knows what people conceal, disclose, and what lies in breasts.
يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ makes a battle encounter of two gathered hosts a named day, the local martial scale behind the section.
When تَرَاءَى الْجَمْعَانِ, the two massed companies see one another, a direct battlefield use of the crowd-root before a decisive encounter.
سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ depicts a confident gathered host suddenly defeated and turning its back, closely matching the vulnerability of the raided crowd.
نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ voices the host's confidence immediately before 54:45 overturns it, sharpening the surprise carried by a crowd's defeat.
The appointed public encounter is يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ when يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى, a worldly day defined by people being assembled at a set time.
فَجُمِعَ السَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقَاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ joins gathering, an appointed time, and a known day on the smaller human stage.
The call هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُجْتَمِعُونَ supplies the public crowd whose appointed gathering is announced in 26:38.
يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ is the recurring human gathering-day named by the same root, a weekly small-scale counterpart to the greatest Day of Gathering.
مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ uses the root for a physical meeting-place, expanding the section's مَجْمَع from gathered people to two seas' confluence.
مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا marks arrival at the place between the two seas, combining meeting-place with the section's developed relation between two sides.
The God-fearing are gathered to the Merciful وَفْدًا, an honored delegation that differentiates one procession within the universal muster.
The guilty are driven to Hell وِرْدًا, reversing the honored delegation of 19:85 and dividing the one gathered humanity by destination.
Those who disbelieved are driven to Hell زُمَرًا; the universal gathering resolves into condemned companies moving to one gate.
Those who feared their Lord are driven to the Garden زُمَرًا, the answering procession and destination opposite 39:71.
On that day people issue أَشْتَاتًا to be shown their deeds: the assembled humanity disperses into distinct parties for disclosure.
On the Day of the Striking Calamity, people become كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ, a scattered visual form of the same resurrected multitude.
When the Hour rises, يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ; the gathering day is also the moment the common crowd separates by outcome.
After the Friday gathering-prayer, فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ sends the congregation outward, the ordinary cycle of gathering followed by dispersal.
A congregation انْفَضُّوا toward trade and leaves the Messenger standing, opposing gathered presence with dispersal driven by worldly provision.
وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ turns the audience from numbered pilgrimage days toward the final gathering to God.
The disbelievers are told they will be overcome and تُحْشَرُونَ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ, giving the assembled movement a defeated destination.
Whether people die or are killed, لَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُحْشَرُونَ relocates every scattered death into one eventual destination.
The hunting rule ends with fear of the God إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, making final assembly the horizon of conduct during earthly gathering and travel.
Birds and earth-creatures are communities like humans and إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ, widening the boundary of creaturely gathering beyond the human crowd.
The warning addresses those who fear أَنْ يُحْشَرُوا إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ without protector or intercessor, emphasizing exposed presence before their Lord.
The command to pray and fear God closes with وَهُوَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, directing the audience toward its common assembly.
The call to respond to God and the Messenger concludes وَأَنَّهُ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, making gathering to Him the audience's final summons.
On the day God gathers them, earthly duration seems one hour and they recognize one another, making the former human crowd fleeting before the final meeting.
The rejected are gathered يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ blind, mute, and deaf, a reversed bodily procession toward Hell.
At the latter promise God brings the addressed people لَفِيفًا, a mixed gathered mass that anticipates the image's enlargement of a local people.
The trumpet is blown and the guilty are gathered that day زُرْقًا, adding a marked bodily condition to the assembled crowd.
The one who turns from remembrance is gathered يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَى, defining an individual's altered place inside the universal assembly.
رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَى lets the gathered person address his Lord from within the condition announced in 20:124.
The one who multiplied people across the earth is also the one وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, reversing earthly dispersal into one destination.
God gathers the worshippers and what they worship, then questions the latter, turning assembly into exposure of who misled whom.
Those gathered عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ form the worst-positioned procession, a judgmental reversal of the charging crowd.
On the day God gathers مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ فَوْجًا of deniers, each cohort is restrained, showing ordered subgroups within the greater muster.
احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا commands the active collection of wrongdoers, their kinds, and their objects of worship for judgment.
After the gathering command of 37:22, this ayah directs the collected company إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ, specifying its destination.
وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَسْئُولُونَ halts the gathered company in compulsory attendance for questioning.
Enemies of God are gathered to the Fire and فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ, held in ordered ranks so none outruns the collective procession.
يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ مِيقَاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ makes the Day of Decision one appointment encompassing every member of the crowd.
God who scattered humanity through the earth declares وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ, compressing terrestrial multiplication back into a single destination.
وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا stages all people exposed before God, after which the weak confront those who had been great.
When earth and heavens are changed, وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ supplies the exposed common presence of the final day.
Every community is seen kneeling and تُدْعَى إِلَى كِتَابِهَا, so the universal crowd becomes distinct peoples summoned to their records.
The book speaks truth over the kneeling communities of 45:28 because their deeds were being copied, explaining what the assembly discloses.
After enumerating religious communities, the ayah says God separates them on Resurrection and is شَهِيدٌ over everything, joining assembled plurality and witness.
The Messenger is شَهِيدًا over the community and they are شُهَدَاءَ over humanity, extending the witness relation of 2:143 without its middle-word.
On the day God raises them جَمِيعًا they swear to Him as they swore to people, while God remains witness over their false performance.
Those who deny are فِي الْعَذَابِ مُحْضَرُونَ, using compulsory presence for the condemned outcome of resurrection.
Those who strive against the signs are فِي الْعَذَابِ مُحْضَرُونَ, another use of being made present as an eschatological destination.
A speaker in Paradise says that without his Lord's favor he would have been مِنَ الْمُحْضَرِينَ, marking the boundary of compulsory presence in punishment.
After Elijah's people reject him, فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ promises their being brought into the judgmental presence.
On that day tongues, hands, and feet تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ, turning each person's own body into witnesses when concealed deeds are exposed.
الْيَوْمَ hands speak and feet تَشْهَدُ, making bodily testimony part of the same day on which everyone is collectively present.
When the gathered enemies reach the Fire, hearing, sight, and skins شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ about their deeds.
The condemned ask their skins لِمَ شَهِدْتُمْ عَلَيْنَا, exposing the unexpected witnesses within their own bodies.
بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ states the self-witnessing relation without the root, matching the human witness of 100:7 at disclosure.
اقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ makes the person sufficient as his own reckoner, a judicial form of witnessing against oneself after inner contents become manifest.
Human descendants are brought forth and made to أَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ, an earlier collective scene of self-testimony before the final gathering.
الصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَى uses the section's middle-root for a prayer situated or valued as the middle, a non-martial application of between-ness.
مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ uses the middle-root for the household's median or fair food, showing the root's evaluative extension from spatial middle.
وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَائِفَةٌ requires a group to be present at a punishment, joining witnessed attendance to an actual gathered public.
The record of the righteous يَشْهَدُهُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ, using witness in the sense of privileged presence around an unveiled record.
الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ applies gathering to hoarded wealth, a telling smaller collection beside God gathering people and what their breasts contain.
وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَى describes one who collects and stores away, opposing private accumulation to the day when persons and hidden contents are collected.
أَلَّنْ نَجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ applies the crowd-root to reassembling one person's bones, the bodily prerequisite of the universal gathering.
النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ presents a human force gathered against the believers; here the crowd is the approaching threat rather than the surprised target.
Pharaoh فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتَى collects his whole stratagem before coming to the appointed public encounter, extending gathering from people to a plan.
Earlier generations stronger in force and أَكْثَرُ جَمْعًا show gathering as amassed worldly resources or followers, which do not prevent divine reckoning.
Divine bounty and mercy are خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ, setting what people accumulate against the final divine collection.
وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ places human accumulation beneath the Lord's mercy, whose authority culminates in gathering them.
Whether people تُخْفُوا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ or reveal it, God knows it, directly anticipating the day's collection of breast-secrets.
God tests مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ and purifies what is in hearts, a process parallel to making their inner contents distinct and manifest.
Even when people fold their breasts to hide, God knows what they conceal and disclose, setting the limit that 100:10's exposure completes.
Concealed or public speech is equally known because God is عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ, matching the Lord's knowledge after inner contents are collected.
God knows treacherous eyes and مَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ, naming precisely the hidden interior that the section says will be gathered out.
Those with disease in their hearts suppose God will not bring out أَضْغَانَهُمْ; the ayah directly promises disclosure of inward contents.
مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ restages the physical meeting implicit in مَجْمَع البحرين without using the gathering-root.
بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ places a boundary between the two meeting seas of 55:19, clarifying that meeting can preserve two sides.
A powerful force جَاسُوا خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ moves through the midst of dwellings, a close nonlexical counterpart to raiders penetrating a settled crowd.
Kings, إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً, ruin it and lower its honored people, spelling out the social reversal implicit when an armed force enters a settlement.
When God's servant stands calling Him, people nearly become لِبَدًا around him, a dense crowd arranged around a central figure.
People enter God's religion أَفْوَاجًا, a peaceful earthly movement of crowds that answers the resurrection crowds arriving after the trumpet.
أَوْسَطُهُمْ may mean the garden owners' most equitable or best member, plausibly extending the middle-root from spatial centrality to balanced judgment.
Attackers come from above and below while the besieged community is caught between them; the link to the section's middle-of-a-crowd raid is specific but nonlexical.
The fortified people are struck from where they did not expect and terror enters their hearts, plausibly echoing the crowd's sudden capture in the raid.
Fighters stand صَفًّا like a solid structure, a plausible ordered counterpart to cavalry breaking into the middle of an opposing gathered force.
